newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan aluminium alloy demand growth seen slowing.
newsitem.headline: Japan aluminium alloy demand growth seen slowing.

text.p: Growth in Japanese demand for aluminium alloy is expected to slow to a slight 0.7 percent in 1997/98, beginning on April 1, from 5.5 percent in 1996/97, the Japan Aluminium Alloy Refiners' Association said on Wednesday.

The association said 1996/97 saw particularly strong demand for aluminium alloy from Japan's carmakers, which registered their first rise in domestic vehicle output in six years due to the weaker yen and a rush of consumer buying ahead of April's national sales tax increase.

While the tax increase was expected to cool the auto sector's demand for forgings and diecast products in 1997/98, the association said this would be cushioned by replacement demand for cars bought at the height of Japan's asset bubble in the late 1980s and by robust exports spurred by the weak yen.
Demand for flat-rolled products was seen ebbing due to the sales tax rise, while a cut in public works spending and dull export markets were likely to erode demand from steelmakers.
